topic.title: [Alopecia areata: recognise, assess, treat]
topic.abstract: Alopecia areata (AA) is an immune-mediated, nonscarring hair disorder with collapse of follicular immune privilege. Diagnosis is based on clinical examination and trichoscopy. Preserved follicular ostia distinguish it from scarring alopecias. The Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score quantifies scalp hair loss, but not activity or burden-both require separate assessment. JAK inhibitors are the first approved systemic therapies. Response follows the hair cycle and can only be judged after 3-6 months. The following apply for children and adolescents: separate algorithms, evidence and approvals are limited, and families should be included in care.
